sections.text: This I have gained today; tomorrow I will gratify another desire; this wealth is mine now, the rest shall be mine ere long;
I have slain one enemy, I will slay the others also; I am worthy to enjoy, I am the Almighty, I am perfect, powerful and happy;
I am rich, I am well-bred; who is there to compare with me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will pay - and I will enjoy. Thus blinded by Ignorance,

We had been discussing chapter 16, Deva Asura Sampada Vibhaga Yoga, Yoga of divine and devilish qualities. And we have seen that these are the qualities of my mind. Even though it seems like it is describing two sets of different people, one are divine and one are devilish.
And as if we are dividing this world again into divine and devilish. The purpose of these qualities to be described in Bhagavad Gita is to understand our own mind. Our own mind has this both qualities, the divine and devilish, depending on which one we promote, either well be liberated or will be bound more and more into this world of limitations.
So the last verse we had seen last time says Asa Pasas Satayi Baddhaha, the person who is not knowledgeable enough about what will liberate him and what will bind him by depending on this notion that the sense enjoyment is the only purpose of life. By hook or crook, I should achieve what I want. They will be more and more bound by unlimited desire, Asha Pasa, bound by this bondage of desires.
You know, satay, that means innumerable desires. And therefore they will do anything which is either appropriate or inappropriate. They will try to achieve, acquire, hoard things which they think will give them the happiness by even illegal means.
Inappropriate means continuing in the same dialogue as we have seen, Bhagavan now describes what will be the tendency or the thinking of these people. Theres not really much to elaborate on it. Just as we have seen that the first three verses which describe the divine quality, there is not really much to be discussed about.
These are universal qualities. Even cavemen knew what is right and wrong. Somebody should not take the food which I have acquired with my labor.
Therefore, if I do that to others, it will be wrong. I dont want somebody to kill me, and therefore killing somebody is bad. These are universal values which every human being from the dawn of the civilization know.
In the same way, the tendencies and thinking of a devilish mind that we are going to be discussing also dont require much explanation. Why? Because we all have experienced this at some point or other, at some level or other. Except that at that time, I did not know that my thinking was going to create more unhappiness for me.
When I was thinking about that, I was thinking Im doing this to get more happiness, for financial security. I put more and more money into the stock market, and as it grows I get the statement every month -- it made 8%, then next month 10%. Feeling pretty good.
Except when it collapsed. Didnt have the courage to open up your statement. But while I was doing that, I thought, Ill get this and then Ill also get this, and therefore Ill be completely secured.
We didnt think it through -- we work all our lives so hard. I have not come across a single person who says, I really need to work hard in my life, but Im enjoying it. Everybody thinks the same thing. What I was thinking all the time was: Idam Adya Maya Labdham -- I have gained this today.
Today I can say I have this. I reconcile my statement of what my assets are at the end of the year, for taxes or whatever. Boy, thats pretty good. Or, Well, at least I have this. And then what is my next thought? Imam Prapsye Manoratham -- I have this, but I will also get this. What if the financial planner says, Okay, well you need to have this to retire at the age of such and such.
This many times your current income -- you will need this, and therefore you need to do the following. So you start planning. The first time a financial planner, a friend of ours coming to Chinmaya Mission in Dallas -- I was pretty young at the time. I was like 30 something.
And he looked at them and said you need million something dollar to retire. I dont think Ill ever have a million dollar. At the time I was probably making like $35,000 a year and the guy was trying to tell me I need million dollar to retire.
You forget about it, okay? Im going to work till I die. No planning required. Because when you see that I have this, I need to achieve this or work hard.
Rajan, you have to have at least this much when you retire. I have this right now. This is a common thinking.
Nobody will label that as devilish. Bhagavan says thats the quality which binds you to this world of constant changes and disappoints you more times than you think it will. Idham asti idam API me bhavishyati punardhanam.
And this wealth shall also be mine in the future. Its simple planning. I acquired this, and Ill work a little hard and do this project, then invest here, and then Ill get that.
Bhagavan says that may be okay for planning purposes, but when that becomes your obsession, then it has a sure capacity for failure. You should be planning. I can never forget this thing in my life.
I bought my first house in Dallas, Texas in 1984, just before the election. I guess it was the Reagan second election. And they told me that after the election the prices will go so out of control that you wont be able to buy.
So you should buy before the election. Says, okay, you buy this house, $150,000 minimum, it will have 5% appreciation. You have compounded 5% for 10 years.
The value of this thing will be this. Oh boy, thats pretty good. They say thats guaranteed 3 to 5%.
It may go up and its guaranteed. I sold that house, the one which I bought in 1984, in 2000. Now you apply that formula, 150,000.
Should have been at least $350,000, right? I sold it for $10,000 more than what I bought in 1984. And as if I have not learned the lesson yet, I bought a house in Northern Virginia where they say it was Dallas. You know, thats an oil dependent economy.
It goes down or it goes up. We are federal government dependent economy. Guaranteed 20% appreciation every year.
You can look at it last five years and you will see it. I bought a house again in 1988, Northern Virginia, in Fairfax. And again I said, well, they say 20%.
Im going to be on 5%. Okay, at least Im safe. I projected in about 10 years, eight years, five years.
I bought it in 1988, sold it in 1996 for exactly $6,000 more than what I had bought for. I made $6,000 after eight years owning that house in Fairfax, Virginia. We plan, but what will come out of my actions is not guaranteed.
Bhagavan said, theres nothing wrong in planning. Thats not in a devilish pursuit. What devilish pursuit is, if this doesnt happen by hook or crook, I will make somebody a Scapegoat and get my money.
So therefore it says Idamasti Idham Apimi Bhavishati Punardhanam. This is mine and this will also be mine. That which I have projected at a 5% appreciation that shall also be mine in 10 years.
I can say this is what I have. This is its value today. What will happen 10 years from now only he knows.
And whoever after 10 years has to buy this house knows. So it is the attitude of my mind makes the same thing either divine or devilish. I took care of this competition.
Obviously in those days they were enemies and they were killing each other. But in a normal day to day even they say I never have killed anybody. So I never said I killed this person.
But we do mentally all the time. I killed this competition. He was trying to be the VP of the company.
But I really manipulated. I went around and talked to all the other bosses and I really pushed him down. And now I got the promotion as vp.
Thats I who killed him for that purpose. So Asaomaya Hataha Satrahu who was my enemy who is in the path of my happiness. My enemy is the one who is obstructing me to be united with my happiness.
I killed this person, initiator Aparanape and the others who I think will be on my way, I will kill them too. It always gives me a kick. Anytime I read this Rasi Bhavishya we get this South Carolina Sati magazine and only thing I read is honestly the horoscope.
Because I have nothing to do with all these businesses in South Carolina. Only thing I can relate to is that last page which says your monthly horoscope. And this guy constantly warns me.
At least the Aries who I am, you know, born in that sign. Be careful about the people around you. They may be planning to harm you.
Now what do you think? My thinking would be well look at Meena, Pourvi, Neeraj, little Medha. They must be all planning something against me or my employees or my friends. This is just insecurity.
We bank on peoples insecurities. Because if you dont take these annuities the market may go down. You will have no security when you are retiring.
You need a guaranteed income. Annuities will give you this guaranteed income. He fails to tell you that those annuities cost lot more than any other investment you would do.
They are making money in your insecurities. What will happen when I return If I dont have money they say okay well take care of it. But well take part of your money and put it in our pocket and make you feel good that you will have the guaranteed income.
I took care of this computation, this enemy, even the others Ill take care of them too. Therefore I will be secured. When Im doing this, my state of my mind is I am the Lord of my being.
I take care of myself. Not only I take care of myself, I take care of all people around me. What would happen to them had I not been doing what I am doing.
All these people are dependent on me. Bhogihi and Im enjoying it. All these efforts which Im putting and gaining this I have got that Ill be getting.
Im the Lord of lord is on whom my existence is dependent on. So in the feudal system whether you live or die, the way you live is dependent on the Lord. He decides how much money there was no unions and nobody decides how much to give it to the workers.
He decides whatever he has to give. So therefore hes the Lord and youre the commoner. Ishwara Same he decides how this world is going to function.
So when I decide that I am the Lord of my Sansar I decide in old Indian system the head of the house will tell how everyone should leave in that house. I think that I control everybody and everything. Bhogi and Im enjoying the fruits of my actions.
Im a successful one. What you have accomplished in your profession and its admirable and what you accomplished in your wealth and its all admirable. Guy doesnt know the other side of the story.
What I not accomplished and where I have failed. It is okay for others to think about that. When I start thinking about my own accomplishments thats where the problem starts.
Its perfectly okay for us to admire the people who accomplished some great things such as Isaac Newton or Bill Gates or Steve Jobs.

These verses expose the inner monologue of the ego-driven mind: This I have gained today; tomorrow I will get more. This wealth is mine; more shall be mine soon. I have defeated this enemy; I will defeat others. I am the lord, the enjoyer, successful, powerful, happy. I am rich and well-born - who is equal to me? Read these statements slowly and notice which ones resonate uncomfortably with your own thought patterns. This is not about shame but honest recognition. When we reconcile our assets, review our accomplishments, or compare ourselves favorably to others, we are walking the edge of this mindset. The teaching does not condemn planning or achievement - it warns against the intoxication that comes when success inflates the ego rather than humbling it.
Verse 15 reveals the final delusion: I will sacrifice, I will give, I will enjoy - even spiritual and charitable acts become corrupted when performed for ego-gratification. The person described here makes donations to see their name on plaques, performs rituals to impress others, and serves the community for recognition. Examine your own generous acts: Do you give anonymously, or do you need acknowledgment? Do you serve quietly, or do you need others to notice? Today, perform one act of kindness or generosity that no one will ever know about. Notice what resistance arises when your ego cannot claim credit. This practice reveals how deeply ajnana (ignorance) has penetrated even our noblest intentions.
